share-bars-wide.lede: A survey with no dependency graph is absent from every share below rather than counted as clean.

figure-band-lead.figures:
[{"lead": "1,161", "label": "carry a known-vulnerable component", "support": "76.8% of surveys whose dependencies a scanner could resolve (1,161 of 1,511)", "tip": "A component with an advisory published against it, matched from the lockfile the project ships. Counted once per survey however many findings it carries.

67.9% of surveys whose dependencies a scanner could resolve (1,026 of 1,511) carry at least one High or Critical.

41.3% of surveys whose dependencies a scanner could resolve (624 of 1,511) carry at least one Critical.

54,141 across 1,511 surveys whose dependencies a scanner could resolve were found across them — three scanners contribute, so a component two of them see is one finding each, while the survey counts above never double-count."}, {"lead": "2,945", "label": "publish no disclosure policy", "support": "83.5% of surveys where the repository itself was checked for a disclosure policy (2,945 of 3,525)", "tip": "No SECURITY.md or security.txt **in the repository itself**. An organisation can publish one policy in its .github repository covering everything it owns, and a project covered that way is reportable while having no file of its own. Nothing here counts those.

90.0% of surveys publishing a disclosure policy (522 of 580) of the policies that do exist name someone to contact."}]
figure-band-lead.footnote: Each is taken over its own population, named beneath it. The four populations are not the same.

share-bars-table.lede: A language is read off the code, so nothing here rests on anybody declaring anything. Affected is taken over each language's own measurable surveys, never over its surveys. 68.3% of surveys in this reading (2,407 of 3,525) could be placed in a language at all; the rest carry no primary language this reading could read, which is a fact about our own indexing and never a fact about the projects.
